bull.b: TTM revenue growth of 64.2% and an 82.6% gross margin show that the commercial base can rebound and retain substantial value per dollar of sales. If sustained, this combination gives Seres more capacity to support its microbiome platform and convert demand into future operating leverage, despite current losses.

The milestone amendment improves funding visibility by exchanging up to $275M of future VOWST milestones for $25M sooner. This brings cash forward to support operations and development over the next several quarters, while reducing reliance on uncertain, later-stage milestone timing as the company advances its portfolio.

SER-155’s early clinical signal provides a potentially meaningful pipeline asset beyond the existing rCDI franchise. An 80% response rate, 33% complete remission, favorable tolerability, and biomarker improvements support continued development and partner discussions, though validation in larger studies remains important.

bear.b: Despite revenue recovery and high gross margin, TTM results remain deeply loss-making, with a net margin around -11.9x revenue and large operating losses. Heavy operating expense relative to sales weakens earnings quality and means growth has not yet translated into a durable, self-sustaining profit engine.

TTM operating and free cash flow are both approximately -$51.3M, showing that the business continues to consume cash rather than fund itself. The reversal from modestly positive 2025 cash flow also indicates unstable cash generation, increasing the importance of external funding or commercial milestones to sustain operations.

Debt of about $56.6M exceeds equity of about $34.5M, while TTM ROE remains negative. Although the balance sheet has improved from earlier stressed periods, elevated leverage and ongoing losses reduce financial flexibility and can constrain investment in clinical programs or commercialization.
